claims.text: High configurational entropy corresponds to a random distribution of five or more elements on a simple lattice.
High configurational entropy preserves robust, isotropic s-wave electron–phonon coupling in the selected HEA.
Configurational disorder stabilizes the local electronic density of states.
Reducing disorder will weaken superconducting pairing or lower Tc.
The selected starting material is a single-phase, fully random, near-equiatomic HEA whose low-temperature superconductivity has not been characterized.

Mild segregation, slight compositional modulation, or thermal treatment can reduce configurational entropy by producing partial short-range ordering while leaving overall stoichiometry approximately constant.
The degree of short-range disorder or ordering controls the density of states at the Fermi level.
The degree of short-range disorder or ordering controls the effective electron–phonon coupling.
Extensive atomic-scale disorder prevents localized electronic states or competing orders from forming.
Preventing localized states or competing orders stabilizes isotropic s-wave pairing.
Lowering mixing entropy alters the Fermi-level density of states and makes electron–phonon coupling less effective at inducing superconductivity.
The reduced-entropy variant will have a lower superconducting transition temperature than the fully disordered control.
The reduced-entropy variant will have a smaller superconducting volume fraction or a less well-defined zero-resistance state than the fully disordered control.
The fully disordered baseline exhibits a superconducting transition around 7–10 K.
A (TaNb)0.67(HfZrTi)0.33 HEA reaches zero resistance near 7.7 K and displays a bulk diamagnetic response near 7.6 K.
Weak-coupling isotropic single-band s-wave superconductivity occurs in (TaNb)1-x(ZrHfTi)x HEA thin films.
The proposed mechanism should apply to structurally similar simple-lattice HEAs when extraneous phases and drastic carrier-concentration changes are absent.
Carrier-concentration variation and lattice strain may affect Tc independently of configurational entropy.

contradictions.description: The starting alloy is described as having uncharacterized superconducting behavior, while the baseline asserts that the same as-synthesized alloy already exhibits a superconducting transition at a given Tc.
